podcast.body: This song was covered by The Dee Gees (Foo Fighters' alter ego) on their 2021 album "Hail Satin." "and one song Shadow Dancing by their brother Andy Gibb."

This song was the Billboard year-end number one for 1978. Co-written with his older brothers Barry, Robin, and Maurice Gibb, it was a "bit of an upset" for Andy to win the year-end title given the dominance of the "Saturday Night Fever" soundtrack. Its blend of "light disco and plush pop" and seven weeks at number one secured its victory. "But Shadow Dancing was the right blend of light disco and plush pop, and its seven weeks on top gave it the win."

podcast.body: This song was the winner of the 1978 Billboard Song of the Summer. Andy Gibb, backed by his Bee Gees brothers, returned with this "sultry" disco song, which was "built for smoldering." According to Billboard, Gibb holds the unique distinction of being the only artist to have the Song of the Summer two years in a row. "One year after, I just want to be your everything, Andy returned, backed by his BG's brothers with his sultry shadow dancing."
